## How PEN is organized

The training has **4 modules**. Modules 1 to 3 each hold a short set of
**units**. Each unit is a recorded video, and some also have slides you can
download. Module 4 is a Resources page you can return to any time. Open a
module below to see what it covers.

<!-- Hand-authored summary of content/modules.yml (title, summary, objectives,
     unit titles, and each module's total video time). If the YAML changes, update
     this block to match. Unit copy elsewhere on this page (the intro and step 2
     below) is deliberately written so it holds whether or not a module has
     slides; Module 2 has none. -->
<div class="module-map">
<p class="module-map-label">Modules 1 to 3: finish these for your certificate</p>
<details><summary><span class="module-map-num" aria-hidden="true">1</span><span><span class="module-map-title"><span class="visually-hidden">Module 1: </span>Getting Started, ADA Insights</span><span class="module-map-meta">4 units, about 57 minutes of video</span></span><span class="module-map-toggle"></span></summary><div class="module-map-body"><p>A plain-language foundation in the ADA: where it came from, what it covers, its five titles, and what it requires, before you look at any data.</p><div class="module-map-cols"><div><h3>You will be able to</h3><ul><li>Place the ADA in its historical context</li><li>Describe the ADA's overall purpose</li><li>Name the five titles and what each covers</li><li>Summarize what the ADA requires</li></ul></div><div><h3>Units</h3><ol><li>ADA History</li><li>Overview of the ADA</li><li>ADA Five Titles</li><li>ADA Requirements</li></ol></div></div></div></details>
<details><summary><span class="module-map-num" aria-hidden="true">2</span><span><span class="module-map-title"><span class="visually-hidden">Module 2: </span>Exploring ADA-PARC Website &amp; Data</span><span class="module-map-meta">3 units, about 51 minutes of video</span></span><span class="module-map-toggle"></span></summary><div class="module-map-body"><p>How the ADA-PARC site is organized: national data, city-level data, and scorecards, so you can find a specific number without a guide.</p><div class="module-map-cols"><div><h3>You will be able to</h3><ul><li>Locate national-level disability data</li><li>Locate city-level data and say how it differs</li><li>Read a scorecard and say what it compares</li></ul></div><div><h3>Units</h3><ol><li>National Data</li><li>City Data</li><li>Scorecards</li></ol></div></div></div></details>
<details><summary><span class="module-map-num" aria-hidden="true">3</span><span><span class="module-map-title"><span class="visually-hidden">Module 3: </span>Making Sense of Data</span><span class="module-map-meta">4 units, about 14 minutes of video</span></span><span class="module-map-toggle"></span></summary><div class="module-map-body"><p>Data literacy for advocacy: what disability data can and cannot tell you, reading numbers versus percentages, and interpreting scorecards responsibly.</p><div class="module-map-cols"><div><h3>You will be able to</h3><ul><li>Explain what a measure is actually counting</li><li>Tell a raw number from a percentage</li><li>Name a limit of national-level data</li><li>Read a scorecard without over-claiming</li></ul></div><div><h3>Units</h3><ol><li>Understanding Data on Disability</li><li>Making Sense of Numbers vs. Percentages</li><li>Limitations of National Data</li><li>How to Make Sense of Scorecards</li></ol></div></div></div></details>
<p class="module-map-label module-map-label-ref">Module 4: use any time, nothing to complete</p>
<details class="module-map-ref"><summary><span class="module-map-num" aria-hidden="true">4</span><span><span class="module-map-title"><span class="visually-hidden">Module 4: </span>Resources</span><span class="module-map-meta">No units</span></span><span class="module-map-toggle"></span></summary><div class="module-map-body"><p>A page to return to after you finish, with links and downloads for using the ADA-PARC data on your own.</p><div class="module-map-cols"><div><h3>What you will find</h3><ul><li>Resource links sorted by category</li><li>The shared Resource Padlet</li><li>A pointer to the glossary</li></ul></div><div><h3>Good to know</h3><ul><li>Not required for your certificate</li><li>No progress to track</li><li>Open it as often as you like</li></ul></div></div></div></details>
</div>

## How a unit works

<ol class="step-list">
<li><span class="step-tag">Step 1</span><div class="step-card"><p class="step-title">Open a module</p><p class="step-text">Start from the home page to see its units.</p></div></li>
<li><span class="step-tag">Step 2</span><div class="step-card"><p class="step-title">Watch a unit</p><p class="step-text">Play the video at your own pace. If the unit has slides, you can download them.</p></div></li>
<li><span class="step-tag">Step 3</span><div class="step-card"><p class="step-title">Mark it complete</p><p class="step-text">Use <strong>Mark unit complete</strong> when you are done with it.</p></div></li>
<li class="step-goal"><span class="step-tag">Step 4</span><div class="step-card"><p class="step-title">Unlock your certificate</p><p class="step-text">Once every unit in Modules 1 to 3 is complete, your certificate unlocks.</p>

## Your progress

<div class="progress-help">
<div class="progress-help-grid">
<div class="progress-help-card">
<h3>What you will see</h3>
<p>Each module shows how many of its units you have completed. For example:</p>
<ul class="progress-help-sample" aria-label="Example progress labels">
<li>Module 2 <span class="status-pill" data-state="todo">Not started</span></li>
<li>Module 3 <span class="status-pill" data-state="in-progress">2 of 4 complete</span></li>
<li>Module 1 <span class="status-pill" data-state="done">Completed</span></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="progress-help-card progress-help-saved">
<h3>Where it is saved</h3>
<p>Only in this browser, on the device you are using. Nothing is sent anywhere.</p>
<p>On a new device, or after you clear your browser data, it starts over. You can mark the units you already finished as complete again.</p>
<p>In a private window, the buttons work for the current visit but are not remembered.</p>
<p>Your Display choices, such as dark colors or larger text, are saved the same way. Clearing your progress does not change them.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="progress-help-reset">
<p>You will be asked to confirm. Clearing removes your completed units and the name on your certificate from this browser.</p>
<button type="button" data-pen-reset class="btn pen-reset-btn">Clear my saved progress</button>
</div>
</div>

## How do I take part with assistive technology?

The site is built to WCAG 2.2 AA. Every page works with the keyboard alone
and with a screen reader. Full detail, and a way to report anything that does
not work, is on the accessibility page.

[Read the accessibility page](accessibility.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg}
